captions.instagram:
50 requests. 100 selects on the same table.

Your auth middleware reads the users row to check whether the account is suspended. It caches it. Then the next helper down the chain selects the same row again, microseconds later, because it has no idea the first one already has it.

Fifteen call sites were paying for that second read — every route with an :id in it.

The fix is not to thread a cached row through fifteen callers. It is one guard inside the function they all already share: check the cache before you select.

Comment CACHE and I'll send the fix.

50 cache misses. 50 identical queries.

The moment a hot key expires, every request in flight misses at once and every one of them goes to the database for the same row.

The cache is not broken. It is empty for a few milliseconds, and that is long enough for fifty callers to walk through the hole.

Store the in-flight promise, not just the result. The first miss loads it and the other forty-nine await the same promise.

1 click. 16 requests.

The gateway retries four times. The client inside it retries four times. One click reaches the service sixteen times.

Every layer that retries multiplies with every other layer that retries, and each one looks reasonable on its own.

Pick one layer to retry at. The edge is usually the right one, and the inner call does zero.

OFFSET counts rows from the top at the moment the query runs. One insert between page one and page two shifts everything down by one.

So row 20 arrives on both pages, and the row that should have been last on page two never appears at all.

Page by the last value you actually saw. The cursor is a row, not a position, so an insert cannot move it.
